subject: tapir
title: A 700-Pound Animal Escapes Predators by Going Underwater

scenes.text: When a predator comes, this 700-pound animal runs straight into a river.
It is a tapir, and it is built for it. Tapirs can swim when they are only a few days old.
It paddles with its head up. But when it needs to hide, it goes under.
The long, flexible snout works like a snorkel, with the nostrils sealed against the water.
It can stay down for several minutes, pushing along the bottom. The river is its safe room.

description:
When a predator shows up, a 700-pound tapir runs into the river.
Its flexible snout works as a snorkel, and it can stay underwater for several minutes.
Would you have guessed this animal was a swimmer?
first_comment: Which land animal would you least expect to be a swimmer? Tell us below.
